transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because... I'm having this issue when I eat. Once I start eating, it feels like I just disappear, almost like something else takes over. And, um, even while I'm in my head telling myself to stop, I just keep going until I can't stand it anymore.
After you eat this way, do you ever do anything to try to make up for it or prevent weight gain?

Yeah. After I eat like that, I usually end up going to a bathroom in my dorm, or sometimes I'll find a quiet floor of the library. And... I make myself throw up. I just get terrified that all that food is just sitting there, turning into weight, so I have to get it out.
How often does this pattern of eating followed by making yourself vomit happen?

Well, um... for most of this semester, it's been happening several times a week. It's definitely not just a once-in-a-while thing anymore. I mean, if I look back over at least the last few months, there really hasn't been a single week where the cycle stopped.
How much do your body shape or weight affect how you judge yourself as a person?

Um, it affects pretty much everything. Like, I can have a decent day in my classes, you know, doing okay with everything else. But if I'm walking back and I catch my reflection in a dorm window... and I think my stomach or my face looks bigger than the other guys around me, it just ruins it all. It feels like I failed at everything. When that happens, I just don't want anyone to see me at all. It's like my weight is the only thing that actually matters about me.

final_diagnosis.reason: Recurrent episodes of uncontrolled binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting, occurring several times weekly for at least several months, with self-worth excessively determined by body shape and weight, support bulimia nervosa.

confirmed_symptoms: Feels unable to stop eating once started despite consciously telling himself to stop
Continues eating until feeling unable to tolerate more
Regularly induces vomiting after binge eating to remove the food and prevent weight gain
Binge-eating and vomiting cycle occurs several times per week
Pattern has continued throughout the last few months without a week-long interruption
Body shape and weight strongly determine self-worth
Perceived weight or appearance changes cause marked distress and feelings of failure
Avoids being seen by others when concerned about appearance

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have occurred several times weekly for most of the semester and at least the last few months.
additional_requirements: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behavior through self-induced vomiting confirmed
Self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body shape and weight
No evidence of significantly low body weight or restrictive anorexia syndrome was provided
